Definition: from G1909 and G191; to hearken (favorably) to:--hear.
BiblicalUsage: Paul quotes Isaiah: I have heard thee in a time accepted, and in the day of salvation have I succoured thee, in 2 Corinthians 6:2 — God heard, and God helped, and now is the accepted time.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God hears in the accepted time, and the accepted time is now — I do not have to wait for a better day to be heard.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
